title: Cerulean Insurance — VPC architecture Q&A and iterative Terraform proposal
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is an internal draft for the Cerulean Insurance private deployment evaluation. Audience: eng-private-deployments, solutions-eng, Cerulean infra/security reviewers. The doc collates sizing estimates, architecture Q&A from the 2025-10-22 scoping call, and an iterative Terraform module approach to speed the first-stage deploy while leaving room for an eventual HA upgrade.

Status summary (short):
- Customer: Cerulean Insurance (mid-sized regional insurer, multi-region AWS, strict data residency: US-East primary, secondary DR US-West).
- Ask: VPC/private deployment of Redwood Inference with model serving cluster inside Cerulean-managed AWS account (no hosted control plane).
- Current state: Proof-of-concept (single node) completed in partner lab. Production reqs: 99.9% uptime, 95th percentile token latency < 180ms for 512-token sequences, throughput ~400 concurrent inference streams (chat) typical, peaks up to 1500 RPS for short-text endpoints.
- This doc: draft sizing + terraform module notes + upgrade plan + unresolved questions.

High-level customer constraints and security requirements:
- Data: all request payloads and logs must stay in Cerulean VPC/subnets; no model inputs leave account.
- Key management: AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs; optional HSM for signing later.
- Network: strict egress rules to only allow our control-plane endpoints (IP allowlist) and S3 endpoints for model artifacts.
- Compliance: SOC2 + internal policy require centralized audit logs to an account-level CloudWatch/CloudTrail bucket and 365-day retention.
- Support window: 24x7 incident escalations with 2-hour response for P1.

Primary technical goals / SLOs:
- Latency: 95p token latency < 180ms for 512 tokens; tail mitigation via KV cache and autoscaling fallback to smaller model variant.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly; multi-AZ preferred but initial GA can be single-AZ with warm standby in secondary AZ.
- Cost target: optimize for mid-range TPU/GPU (A10G or A100 small clusters) with quantized 4-bit variants where quality acceptable.

Workload profile (from Cerulean telemetry + questionnaire):
- Steady: 400 concurrent chat sessions, ~0.8 requests/sec per session average.
- Peak daily bursts: 08:00–10:00 local (~x3 baseline) for claims intake.
- Typical prompt size: 120–300 tokens. Long-form generation rare (512 tokens).
- Model candidates: open llama-70b-qat-4bit (quantized) for cost, fallback to 13b FP16 for sub-100ms cases.

Sizing estimate (initial prod lane, safety headroom included) — conservative numbers to start:
- Serving nodes: 8 GPU hosts across 2 AZs (4 hosts per AZ). Host type recommendation: p4d-lite (A10G equivalent) or g5.2xlarge equivalent if A100 not necessary — tradeoffs below.
  - GPUs per host: 1xA10G or 1xA100-small (depends on model choice).
  - Memory: 512Gi host RAM target for caching and k-v store.
  - Disk: 1.5Ti NVMe local for model shards + 3Ti EBS gp3 per instance for checkpoints/log buffering.
- Inference capacity rough math: each A10G host (with 4-bit quant) ~ 180–220 tok/s for 512-token seqs (approx). 8 hosts -> ~1.6k tok/s. With average request token consumption ~100 tokens -> ~16 requests/sec sustained, but batching and multiple concurrent streams increase throughput. We rely on batching + KV cache to hit customer RPS peaks.
- KV cache nodes: 3 x m6i.large in a private autoscaling group to host shared prefix caches (stateless pods can attach).
- Control plane (customer-managed): 2 t3.large EC2 for control-plane agent, autoscaled replicas managed by ASG but behind internal ELB.
- Bastion + Ops: 1x t3.medium for jump host, 1x m5.large for logging agent/forwarder.

Cost/perf tradeoffs and recommendations:
- If Cerulean prioritizes latency and is willing to pay, use A100-small (higher raw perf, lower batch-latency) and fewer nodes.
- If cost-sensitive, use A10G + 4-bit quant with more aggressive batching and per-request timeouts to avoid tail latencies.
- Suggest initial rollout with 8 A10G hosts and telemetry-driven scaling rules for first 90 days, revisit after workload telemetry.

Networking topology (proposal):
- VPC with 3 private subnets across 2 AZs (primary and secondary AZ). Public subnets for NAT/egress-only endpoints.
- Internal NLB in front of serving nodes for internal clients (the NLB is within Cerulean account).
- Private S3 endpoints for model artifact fetch; Terraform will create IAM roles for instance profile access scoped to artifact prefixes.
- Control-plane connectivity: lightweight agent pulls config from a customer-managed SQS queue and polls an S3 manifest. Only whitelisted Redwood control-plane IPs allowed.
- Security groups: strict SG design with least privilege; SG for serving hosts only allow NLB and certain monitoring ports.

Terraform module approach (iterative):
Goal: deliver a safe, repeatable set of TF modules that Cerulean can own. We propose a three-phase plan:
Phase 0: bootstrap (quick, minimal):
  - Modules: network-bootstrap (VPC, subnets, route tables), iam-bootstrap (roles for instances, S3 access), s3-artifacts (bucket policies), state-backend (S3 + dynamodb).
  - Keep modules small and parameterized; avoid opinionated autoscaling rules.
Phase 1: serving-core (initial prod):
  - Modules: serving-ecs-or-k8s (decide runtime strategy), instance-profile, launch-configuration, autoscaling-groups, internal-nlb, kms-integration, logging-forwarder.
  - Use remote state locked with DynamoDB.
  - Version modules as semver and publish to our internal module registry; reference via git tags in Cerulean's infra repo.
Phase 2: ha-and-upgrade (HA/upgrade playbook):
  - Modules: cross-az-autoscaler, canary-traffic-shift (route53 weighted records), blue-green-deploy-helper (pre-warm nodes and model cache), hsm-connector.

Terraform specifics / notes: 
- State: separate state per environment (dev/stage/prod) and per major component (network vs compute). We recommend encryption at rest using CMK.
- Module inputs to parameterize heavily: gpu_type, gpu_count_per_host, model_artifact_s3_prefix, instance_ami, user_data_template, kms_key_arn, allowed_controlplane_ips.
- Resource lifecycle: use create_before_destroy for auto-scaling-group replacements where possible; have graceful drain scripts for terminating instances to persist caches to S3 if needed.
- Drift: add periodic terraform plan automation via pipeline job in Cerulean CI to detect drift; script to reconcile common tags/policies.

Runtime decisions to finalize with customer:
- Kubernetes vs ECS vs raw EC2 for serving:
  - Kubernetes (EKS): better for pod-level isolation, can use device plugin for GPUs; more Ops overhead but aligns with Cerulean's standard.
  - EC2 ASG with supervised container runtime: simpler initial deploy, less surface area for kube upgrades.
  - Recommendation: EKS if Cerulean already runs EKS in prod (they do) — deliver an EKS-based module. Otherwise, EC2 ASG for fastest time to prod.

Upgrade and rollback plan (high-level):
- Canary/blue-green approach: always pre-pull model artifacts to new nodes, pre-warm KV caches with representative prompts, run a set of canary traffic (1–5% of production) for 15–30 minutes. If telemetry is within thresholds, shift weighted route to new nodes.
- Rollback: weighted shift back to previous deployment; terminate new nodes with create_before_destroy disabled until traffic reduced to zero.
- DB/migrations: none for core serving. Ensure logging schema backward compatibility.
- Version pinning: allow customers to pin model version + runtime image; default to our vetted image tag and provide an override variable.

Operational runbooks (summary):
- P1 outage: failover to secondary AZ by scaling up warm standby hosts there; if capacity exhausted, automatic fallback to lower-cost smaller model variant in emergency mode.
- Memory pressure: if KV cache eviction sees >25% miss rate increase, autoscale more hosts and reduce batch windows for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Disk fill: rotate model artifacts to S3; alert at 75% disk use.

Security & compliance notes:
- Use customer CMK for EBS and S3 encryption. Terraform module will require kms_key_arn param and will not create CMK by default.
- Audit logs: forward CloudTrail + application logs to a central Cerulean bucket; we will provide the logging-forwarder module to manage Kinesis/CloudWatch subscription.
- Secrets: rely on AWS Secrets Manager or parameter store; no plaintext credentials in TF.

Open questions (needs answers from Cerulean):
1) EKS adoption: confirm whether Cerulean wants EKS for ML infra or prefers ASG/EC2 approach. (Action: Solutions Eng to confirm by 2026-03-05).
2) Control plane allowlist: can Cerulean accept the Redwood control-plane IPs for agent checkout? If not, discuss VPN/PrivateLink connector.
3) HSM: is HSM mandatory for signing and key operations or optional? Impact on timeline if mandatory.
4) Expected retention/ingestion of request logs for 365 days — confirm budget for S3 costs.
5) Acceptable quantization/quality threshold — Cerulean must run evals to accept 4-bit quant model variants.

Action items / next steps:
- [Maya] Draft initial terraform repo skeleton and push bootstrap modules (due 2026-03-08).
- [Diego] Run a perf matrix for A10G vs A100 on the selected model (LLM-70B-4bit) with Cerulean sample prompts (due 2026-03-10).
- [Aisha] Schedule security kickoff with Cerulean infra team to lock down KMS/HSM requirements and SPLs (due 2026-03-04).
- [Benji] Prepare an EKS module variant + minimal EC2 fallback module; include user_data scripts for model prefetch and graceful drain (due 2026-03-15).

Notes on telemetry & readouts to measure post-deploy:
- Daily: 95p token latency, model cache hit ratio, average batch size, tokens/sec per host.
- Weekly: cost per 1M tokens, autoscale events, disk churn.
- Monthly: availability vs target, regression alerts for quality.

Appendix: quick checklist for first deploy
- [ ] Cerulean to create S3 bucket for artifacts + provide prefix + grant cross-account role to Redwood deploy agent.
- [ ] Cerulean to provide CMK ARN for state & EBS encryption.
- [ ] Cerulean to confirm EKS vs EC2 runtime choice.
- [ ] Agree on allowed control-plane IPs (or plan PrivateLink design).
- [ ] Execute pilot with 2 nodes in primary AZ + 1 warm in secondary AZ for two weeks.

Meeting notes excerpt (2025-10-22 call):
- Cerulean security: "We cannot permit any outbound to third-party model registries; artifacts must be in our account."
- Product: "We need the ability to pin model version and run automatic rollback if quality drops during rollout."
- Ops: "We run EKS across the account; if you can provide an EKS chart we can adopt it into our cluster infra."

Comments (freeform):
- This doc purposely leaves several knobs for Cerulean to control (KMS, EKS, state). The TF modules should err on side of configurable rather than opinionated defaults.
- We should prepare a short evaluation harness (Jupyter + small dataset) for them to run quantized model quality checks before any wide rollouts.

End of draft.
